summary:
Crew Swap is a mission-readiness web console that helps a Mars-transit crew turn sleep and fatigue evidence into duty decisions, then replan work when someone stands down.

We built a browser app with a Node local server: operators review BIDSleep-based sleep trends and check-ins, see an auto-flag grounded in short-sleep rules, confirm stand-down or availability as medical officer, and reassign (or defer) a cooling-loop inspection when coverage breaks. Editable skills, a decision log, an Earth handoff packet, and a Gemini-powered mission chat complete the loop.

It addresses the challenge of keeping crews safe and productive under fatigue and delayed Earth support—by pairing real sleep data with human confirmation and immediate ops replanning, not silent automation. That matters for long-duration spaceflight and Earth analogs: better duty clearance reduces risk while preserving mission coverage.
details:
Crew Swap is a mission-readiness web console for a fictional Mars-transit crew. It helps operators turn sleep and fatigue data into clear duty decisions, then replan work when someone cannot fly the next task.

What it does / how it works
 Operators follow a four-step loop:

  1. Gather — review measured sleep trends (from open PhysioNet BIDSleep data) and self-reported check-ins.
  2. Flag — an auto-score uses latest sleep, personal baseline, nights under 6 hours, and derived fatigue (NASA-aligned short-sleep rules). Score ≥4 recommends stand-down; 2–3 is watch.
  3. Confirm — a human (crew medical officer; commander reviews the medical officer) confirms available or stand-down.
  4. Act — if coverage breaks, reassign a cooling-loop inspection (or defer), bump the plan version, log the decision, and prepare an Earth handoff packet.

Crew skills and inspection requirements are editable, so eligibility is not locked to fixed role labels. A floating Mission chat answers questions about the live mission state (Gemini by default, with local fallback / optional OpenAI).

Benefits

  • Makes fatigue risk visible before a high-stakes task
  • Keeps a human in the loop (no silent auto-stand-down)
  • Shows the operational cost of a stand-down (coverage gaps, reassignment, deferred work)
  • Leaves an auditable decision log and Earth packet for remote review
  • Uses real open sleep measurements instead of invented numbers alone

Intended impact
 Demonstrate how deep-space and long-duration crews (and Earth analogs) could pair biomedical sleep evidence with ops replanning when communication delay makes Earth real-time oversight hard. The prototype argues for safer duty clearance: measure → flag → human confirm → replan.

Tools, languages, hardware, software

  • Languages: HTML, CSS, JavaScript (vanilla front end); Node.js (server.cjs) for local static serving + /api/chat; Python (tools/import_sleep.py) to import BIDSleep .mat labels into sleep totals
  • Data: PhysioNet BIDSleep (open dataset); simulated crew names, roles, and Mars schedule
  • AI: Google Gemini (default live chat), optional OpenAI; env/.env configuration
  • Runtime: Local browser app on http://127.0.0.1:43730 (Windows/macOS/Linux via npm start or launcher scripts)
  • No special hardware — runs on a standard laptop/desktop

How it’s creative
 It treats crew health and mission planning as one story, not two dashboards: a stand-down is not just a status badge—it forces a coverage choice. Real sleep science (BIDSleep + short-sleep thresholds) drives a sci‑fi ops console with editable qualifications, decision logging, and an in-console AI assistant that knows the current crew state.

Factors the team considered

  • Safety vs automation: recommend stand-down, never auto-remove people without confirmation
  • Evidence integrity: prefer measured sleep over purely fictional fatigue
  • Operational realism: qualifications, commander/specialist requirements, deferral when no one is eligible
  • Usability under stress: clear Gather → Flag → Confirm → Act path; alert banner; mission chat for guidance
  • Privacy / ethics: open research sleep data; fictional crew identities; local-first demo
  • Latency / deep space context: Earth packet assumes delayed handoff, not instant Earth micromanagement
  • Demo reliability: works offline with local chat; live AI when an API key is configured
